messages:
maya: Quick design sync 12: Prompt Sets -> Eval Runs list update. I uploaded a new prototype that reflows the regression diffs into a two-pane list (left: run meta, right: diff preview) and collapses the old floating approve CTA into a persistent toolbar action. Need accessibility and copy review before I freeze for dev. https://figma.com/file/abc
sam: Nice direction. Two-pane feels more scan-able. Concern: it may push important metadata below the fold on small screens. How does it behave at 1024px width?
maya: At 1024px it stacks vertically (meta on top, preview below). I added a responsive rule to switch to single-column at <= 1100px.
jorge: Suggestion: keep the run status badges (Approved / Needs Review / Regression) pinned so they never reflow offscreen. Users rely on those at a glance.
rita: Accessibility: ensure the two-pane is exposed as a single list item to assistive tech, not two separate list widgets. Use role="list" with role="listitem" for rows and aria-labelledby linking to the title.
ux-bot: accessibility note: When the diff preview updates (on expand), announce "Diff preview opened for run X" using aria-live polite. Also ensure keyboard users can expand/collapse with Enter/Space.
sam: Microcopy: toolbar approve action label 12: present "Approve selected". Avoid verbs like "bulk". Include a tooltip: "Approve selected eval runs and lock scorecards".
maya: Good call. Also thinking to change confirmation modal copy from generic "Are you sure?" to: "Approve 3 runs? This will mark results as approved and prevent further edits unless unapproved by a project admin"
jorge: Who can unapprove? Product says project admins only. If so, modal should mention "Only project admins can unapprove" with link to docs.
rita: Also require contextual aria-describedby pointing to the modal detail text so screen readers read the consequences.
sam: Visual NIT: selection checkbox is currently 18px. Increase to 24px for hit target and touch. Add clear visual state for indeterminate when partial selection.
maya: Will update. UX question: where to surface per-run confidence/quality metrics? Right now only visible in expanded diff. Should we show a small sparkline or score chip in the list row?
jorge: Tiny score chip (0-100) with color coding makes sense. Use sufficient contrast and include hidden text like "Quality score: 86" for screen readers.
ux-bot: contrast check: green chips on light background pass AA only if text is 14px bold. Consider HC icon alternative for small sizes.
sam: Another keyboard flow: a user can open first run, press "j/k" to navigate runs, but when focus is inside diff textarea the nav hijacks. Recommend scoping global nav shortcuts to when focus is on the list container only.
rita: Also run an RTL test for the layout since some customers will run in Arabic/Hebrew. Two-pane should flip gracefully.
maya: Thanks. I'll implement: pinned status badges, 24px checkboxes, revised modal copy with admin unapprove note + docs link, aria-live announcements, increased hit targets for expand chevrons, and scoped keyboard shortcuts.
jorge: One last microcopy nudge: change "View changes" action in the toast to "Open change log" so it's clearer that it's a history view, not in-line edits.
sam: And add small divider and hover surface in roomy layout; in compact layout remove divider and use background tint on hover.
maya: Perfect. I'll update prototype and post new figma by EOD. Rita: can you run keyboard-only pass and paste steps here so we can handoff a11y checklist to eng?
rita: Yep, will do and include screenreader narration examples.
maya: Thanks everyone!
